Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 42, verses 1–6:

The disjointed letters (muqatta'at) at the beginning of several surahs have already been discussed earlier, so there is no need to repeat it here. These letters indicate that the surah is beginning. The first statement after these letters is:

﴿Thus does Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, reveal (to you and) to those who were before you﴾ (42:3): "Thus Allah, the Mighty and Wise, has been revealing to you and to the Messengers who passed before you." That is, just as revelation is coming to you, in the same manner We have sent revelation to the earlier Messengers too. This revelation has consisted of words, expressions and the letters of the alphabet. The word of Allah has been formed from letters. People are well acquainted with these letters, and they understand the meanings of these words, but like this revelation they cannot produce such speech, even though the material from which this speech is made lies before them and within their reach.

The second meaning of this is that revelation is one; its source and origin is one Allah, who is Mighty and Wise. And those to whom revelation comes are the Messengers of every time and place. The Messengers differ; differences of time and place may exist, but revelation and guidance are one and the same.

﴿to you and to those before you﴾ (42:3): "to you and to the Messengers who passed before you."

This is a very long story, with many threads of the ups and downs of time and countless links of history, but the principle of revelation is one firm and enduring method, and it has many branches.

When this idea settles in the hearts of the believers in this manner, they come to feel that the path and method they follow is one permanent, single way, its source is also the One Allah alone, and that their lineage too goes back to Allah, the Mighty, the Forbearing. In this way there also arises in them the consciousness that they are members of a historic caravan of truth, whose last link and first link stretch far back within time and space. It is as if the believers form one family whose spiritual genealogy begins from the very dawn of human history. At the end, the links of this lineage meet and all of them arrive at Allah, the Mighty, who is Powerful and Absolute, who is Wise, and who, with His wisdom and planning, reveals to whomever He wills. Therefore, why are you scattering away from this single, firm and permanent divine method and wandering along various footpaths? For these footpaths do not lead to Allah; neither is their starting point known, nor their destination, nor is their path straight.

Allah, who revealed to all the Messengers, is further described as the One to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Exalted, the Great.

﴿To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ (42:4).

Sometimes people are deceived and think that they too are owners, merely because they see these things in their hands, under their control. They benefit from them and make use of them as they wish. But this is not true ownership. True ownership belongs to Allah. It is He who brings into existence and annihilates, gives life and causes death. It is He who gives to whomever He wills among mankind, and deprives whomever He wills of whatever He wills. At the time He wills, whatever is in their hands suddenly departs, and if He wills, He gives a replacement for what has gone. The true Owner of all things is Allah; He runs these things according to His law of nature, and all these things respond to His command. In this sense, whatever is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Allah, and in this sense no one shares ownership with Allah.

﴿And He is the Most High, the Most Great﴾ (42:4): He is not only the Owner, He is also the Supreme Owner, and He is free of all in His greatness. He is exalted in such a way that everything is lesser in comparison to Him, and He is great in such a sense that everything is very small in comparison to Him.

When this reality is firmly established in the constitution of human beings, and people come to know that the wealth, provision and livelihood they seek for their souls must be sought from the right source, namely that Allah is the Owner of whatever is in the heavens and the earth, and only the Owner can give anything to anyone; further, He is Exalted and Great, so if someone asks Him for something, He does not reject their request. Whereas when we extend our hands before creatures, they are neither exalted nor great, and therefore their requests may be denied.

After this, a scene from this universe is shown which makes clear that the Owner of this universe is Allah alone, and that loftiness and greatness belong to Allah alone: ﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them﴾ because of the awe of Allah's majesty, and because of the deviation and evil words of some people. Furthermore, as a manifestation of Allah's greatness, it is also brought here that the angels constantly glorify Allah with praise and seek forgiveness for the people of the earth, because on seeing the deviation and misguidance of the people of the earth, they too are overwhelmed with awe.

﴿The heavens are almost rent asunder from above them, and the angels glorify the praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on the earth. Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (42:5).

The heavens are the vast universe that is visible above us. Wherever we are on the back of this globe, and whatever information we have gathered so far about it, that information concerns only a very small part of it. According to the information available until today, we have learned that there exist a hundred thousand million suns like our sun, together with their countless satellites. And how many such clusters or groups are there? About a hundred thousand million groups have been identified. It should be remembered that this sun is a million times larger than our earth. And these hundreds of billions of suns are only those we observe through our small observatories; they are scattered within this boundless cosmic space (which we call the sky), and between them are vast distances, many millions of light-years away, which are measured according to the speed of light, that is, at 186,000 miles per second.

These heavens, about which our knowledge is very limited, are almost rent asunder above us in this atmosphere. Why? Out of fear of Allah, out of the greatness of Allah and out of the majesty of Allah, and because of the evil deeds of the people of the earth, their heedlessness and forgetfulness regarding that Lord of Majesty and this universe. The heavens are almost struck with trembling, and they may break apart and fall from the place where they are fixed.

﴿And the angels glorify the praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on the earth﴾ (42:5). The angels are a creation that is entirely obedient. They are the best of all creation, yet they constantly glorify their Lord, because they know how exalted and how great their Lord is. Despite their complete obedience, they still fear that some shortcoming may occur in their praise and obedience. Whereas the people of the earth are both sinners and weak, they have deviated from the right path, and yet they do not feel it. Therefore the angels fear the wrath of Allah, and regarding the disobedience and shortcomings that occur on earth, they seek forgiveness out of fear of Allah's wrath. It may also be that the angels' seeking forgiveness here means seeking forgiveness for the believers, as mentioned in Surah Ghafir:

﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify the praise of their Lord and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾ (40:7). From this condition it becomes clear that the angels greatly fear the commission of disobedience on earth. Even if believers commit disobedience, the angels fear, and out of that fear they seek forgiveness from Allah for the people of the earth, and they continually declare His purity along with praise of Him, so that because of those disobediences Allah's punishment does not come, and so that Allah's mercy keeps descending upon people. They hope that people will be forgiven and that mercy will be shown to them.

﴿Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (42:5). Along with the attributes of might and wisdom, and the attributes of loftiness and greatness, the attributes of forgiveness and mercy are also gathered here, so that people keep all the attributes of their Lord in view.

At the end of this passage, after the description of these divine attributes and their effects in this universe, the address turns to those who have taken other protectors besides Allah, although it has already been made clear that there is no protector in this universe except Allah. This is so that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may now disengage from their affairs, since he has not been appointed as their guardian. Allah alone is truly their watcher and controller.

﴿And those who have taken protectors other than Him—Allah is Guardian over them; and you are not over them a manager﴾ (42:6). In the human imagination there comes the picture of these perverse and wretched people who have stretched out their hands before protectors other than Allah and ask something from them, while their hands are empty; there is nothing there but wind. The picture of them and the picture of their protectors is an extremely repugnant, contemptible and diminutive picture. These people are in the power of Allah and are extremely small. The Prophet ﷺ has been told that he is free of responsibility for their affairs. He should not concern himself with them; Allah will take care of them.

This matter should be firmly settled in the hearts of the believers, and they should be content in this matter, in every condition. Whether those taken as protectors are rulers and people of power and position on this earth, or others, the believers should be content in the following way regarding rulers: however tyrannical and oppressive they may be, if their authority is not derived from the Qur'an and Sunnah, then they are within Allah's grip; Allah has encompassed them. The whole universe around them believes in Allah; only they have deviated. They are like a harsh voice in a most harmonious melody. And if these protectors are other than rulers, such as saints or spiritual leaders, then the believers bear no responsibility for them, because if anyone among Allah's creatures adopts a wrong path, it is not their responsibility. There is no compulsion in religion and beliefs; upon them rests only the duty of conveying the message. Allah alone is the watcher over the hearts of His servants.

Therefore, the duty of believers is to walk on their straight path in the light of divine revelation, and if other people adopt wrong beliefs, the believers bear no responsibility for that. Whatever those wrong beliefs may be, they themselves are responsible for them. Now we come to the first theme of this surah, namely revelation and prophethood:

Furthermore, as a manifestation of Allah's greatness, it is also brought here that the angels constantly glorify Allah with praise and seek forgiveness for the people of the earth, because on seeing the deviation and misguidance of the people of the earth, they too are overwhelmed with awe.

The heavens are the vast universe that is visible above us. Wherever we are on the back of this globe, and whatever information we have gathered so far about it, that information concerns only a very small part of it. According to the information available until today, we have learned that there exist a hundred thousand million suns like our sun, together with their countless satellites. And how many such clusters or groups are there? About a hundred thousand million groups have been identified. It should be remembered that this sun is a million times larger than our earth. And these hundreds of billions of suns are only those we observe through our small observatories; they are scattered within this boundless cosmic space (which we call the sky), and between them are vast distances, many millions of light-years away, which are measured according to the speed of light, that is, at 186,000 miles per second.

These heavens, about which our knowledge is very limited, are almost rent asunder above us in this atmosphere. Why? Out of fear of Allah, out of the greatness of Allah and out of the majesty of Allah, and because of the evil deeds of the people of the earth, their heedlessness and forgetfulness regarding that Lord of Majesty and this universe. The heavens are almost struck with trembling, and they may break apart and fall from the place where they are fixed.

﴿And the angels glorify the praise of their Lord and ask forgiveness for those on the earth﴾ (42:5). The angels are a creation that is entirely obedient. They are the best of all creation, yet they constantly glorify their Lord, because they know how exalted and how great their Lord is. Despite their complete obedience, they still fear that some shortcoming may occur in their praise and obedience. Whereas the people of the earth are both sinners and weak, they have deviated from the right path, and yet they do not feel it. Therefore the angels fear the wrath of Allah, and regarding the disobedience and shortcomings that occur on earth, they seek forgiveness out of fear of Allah's wrath. It may also be that the angels' seeking forgiveness here means seeking forgiveness for the believers, as mentioned in Surah Ghafir:

﴿Those who bear the Throne and those around it glorify the praise of their Lord and believe in Him, and ask forgiveness for those who believe﴾ (40:7). From this condition it becomes clear that the angels greatly fear the commission of disobedience on earth. Even if believers commit disobedience, the angels fear, and out of that fear they seek forgiveness from Allah for the people of the earth, and they continually declare His purity along with praise of Him, so that because of those disobediences Allah's punishment does not come, and so that Allah's mercy keeps descending upon people. They hope that people will be forgiven and that mercy will be shown to them.

﴿Unquestionably, Allah is the Forgiving, the Merciful﴾ (42:5). Along with the attributes of might and wisdom, and the attributes of loftiness and greatness, the attributes of forgiveness and mercy are also gathered here, so that people keep all the attributes of their Lord in view.

At the end of this passage, after the description of these divine attributes and their effects in this universe, the address turns to those who have taken other protectors besides Allah, although it has already been made clear that there is no protector in this universe except Allah. This is so that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ may now disengage from their affairs, since he has not been appointed as their guardian. Allah alone is truly their watcher and controller.

﴿And those who have taken protectors other than Him—Allah is Guardian over them; and you are not over them a manager﴾ (42:6). In the human imagination there comes the picture of these perverse and wretched people who have stretched out their hands before protectors other than Allah and ask something from them, while their hands are empty; there is nothing there but wind. The picture of them and the picture of their protectors is an extremely repugnant, contemptible and diminutive picture. These people are in the power of Allah and are extremely small. The Prophet ﷺ has been told that he is free of responsibility for their affairs. He should not concern himself with them; Allah will take care of them.

This matter should be firmly settled in the hearts of the believers, and they should be content in this matter, in every condition. Whether those taken as protectors are rulers and people of power and position on this earth, or others, the believers should be content in the following way regarding rulers: however tyrannical and oppressive they may be, if their authority is not derived from the Qur'an and Sunnah, then they are within Allah's grip; Allah has encompassed them. The whole universe around them believes in Allah; only they have deviated. They are like a harsh voice in a most harmonious melody. And if these protectors are other than rulers, such as saints or spiritual leaders, then the believers bear no responsibility for them, because if anyone among Allah's creatures adopts a wrong path, it is not their responsibility. There is no compulsion in religion and beliefs; upon them rests only the duty of conveying the message. Allah alone is the watcher over the hearts of His servants.

Therefore, the duty of believers is to walk on their straight path in the light of divine revelation, and if other people adopt wrong beliefs, the believers bear no responsibility for that. Whatever those wrong beliefs may be, they themselves are responsible for them. Now we come to the first theme of this surah, namely revelation and prophethood:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran (Urdu translation)) on surah 42, verse 7–9 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 7 to 9

﴿And thus have We revealed to you an Arabic Qur'an﴾ (42:7), "Yes, in this way, O Prophet, We have revealed to you this Qur'an in Arabic."

So that you may warn the central city of the towns, Makkah, ﴿and those around it﴾ (42:7).

This sentence is a continuation (ma'tuf) of the sentence with which the surah begins, that is, of "Thus does He reveal" (kadhalika yuha). The "thus" (kadhalika) at the beginning of the surah referred to the muqatta'at (the disjointed letters). Here the connection between the continuation and that which it continues is the connection between the disjointed letters and the Arabic Qur'an. This connection is evident: those letters are Arabic, and this is an Arabic Qur'an. Revelation made this Qur'an from those letters so that it might fulfil its purpose. And what is its aim and goal?

﴿So that you may warn the mother of the cities and those around it﴾ (42:7), "So that you may warn the central city of the towns (Makkah) and those who live around it."

Umm al-Qura refers to Makkah Mukarramah. In it was the House of Allah, the ancient house of God. Allah chose that the Ka'bah should be the centre of this final message, and Allah chose the Arabic language for His final Book. This was His wisdom, and He alone knows why.

﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ (6:124), "Allah alone knows best where to place His message."

When today we examine historical events, and survey the whole of history, and observe the circumstances and requirements of that time, then we see how this call spread, along which lines it advanced, what results it produced, and what effects it left upon the world. When we make this survey today, we come to know why Allah chose this land for that purpose, and why, at a particular turn of history, He made Makkah Mukarramah the centre for this final message. Since this final message was indeed a universal message, meant for all mankind, and its universal features were evident from its earliest days.

At the time of the emergence of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the inhabited regions of the whole globe were divided among four emperors. The Roman empire, which ruled over a part of Asia and over Africa. The kingdom of the Persian Kisra, whose power was established over a large part of Asia and a part of Africa, the kingdom of India, and the kingdom of China. These last two empires were enclosed within their own shells; they had their own beliefs, and there were only political ties between China and India. Because the kingdoms of China and India were enclosed within their own shells, the real influence upon the societies of the world belonged to the governments of the Caesar of Rome and the Kisra of Persia.

In that age there were two well-known heavenly religions in the world: Judaism and Christianity. Both these religions had reached a position where each had come under the influence of some government and kingdom. The influence of government had been established over these religions. The kingdom was not under the influence of religion; rather, the kingdom dominated religion. This was because distortion and alteration had occurred within these religions, and their adherents had become corrupt in conduct.

The Jews were oppressed at one time by the Romans and at another by the Persians. They had no notable position in that region. Circumstances had compelled Judaism to become merely the religion of the Jews, that is, the Children of Israel, and to shrink within itself. They neither needed nor desired to bring other nations into the religion of Judaism.

As for present-day Christianity, it was produced by the Roman kingdom. When Christianity came into existence, the Roman kingdom was in power over Palestine, Egypt, Syria and the other regions in which Christianity had spread secretly, and the Roman kingdom was persecuting it. The followers of this religion were hunted and subjected to hardships. This persecution was so severe that thousands of people were slaughtered in a cruel manner. When this period of persecution ended and the Caesar of Rome himself entered the religion of Christianity, he brought with him idolatrous myths as well. Thus the mythological philosophies of Greece entered Christianity, and the simple form of Christianity was altered. Consequently, the Christianity that came into being under the shadow of the state was entirely different from the religion that Allah revealed to Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him); rather, a new thing came into being. What happened was that the Roman kingdom recited the creed, but it was not affected by Christianity. Meanwhile, Christianity, which had not been brought under control by persecution, now came completely under control. Because of this state control, the religion broke into even more pieces, and thus a second period of persecution began: official Christianity started crushing other sects. The church was divided, and there arose the danger that the Roman kingdom itself would be divided as a result. Thus one official sect crushed the other sects, and the condition of both became such that none of them remained upon the religion of Hadrat Isa.

This was the time when Islam appeared. The aim of Islam was that humanity, which was trapped in deviation, corruption, oppression and ignorance, should be brought out of those darknesses. Islam desired to take the whole of human life under its control and to guide it upon the most luminous and correct path. It was necessary that Islam establish its supreme authority over all of humanity, so that the great revolution that Islam had in view could be brought into human life. Therefore it was necessary that Islam begin from a place that was free, and where none of the great empires of the world held power. And that the growth and development of Islam take place in circumstances in which no state would be imposed upon it that was contrary to its nature, but rather that Islam itself would be in power over that region. Keeping these aims in view, if one considers, then Makkah Mukarramah, according to the circumstances of that time, was an excellent place for the beginning of Islam, from where Islam began its universal journey, because a universal revolution was from the first day in view for Islam.

In the Arabian Peninsula in those days there was no organised government with its own laws, its own armies, its own police, which held authority over the entire Arabian Peninsula and which, relying upon its organised structure, could confront a new system of life. And the common people were not fully under its control, as was the case with the four empires of the world at that time.

Furthermore, there was no clear religion in the Arabian Peninsula such as Judaism and Christianity were, nor was there a scattered idolatry of a single kind. The beliefs and ways of life of the tribes were different. Their deities were also different: from angels, from jinn, from planets and stars, and from idols. Nevertheless, despite these circumstances, the Ka'bah and the religious leadership and dominance of the Quraysh were accepted throughout the Arabian Peninsula. Although this leadership was not a formal sovereign authority, neither in Makkah nor outside Makkah. For this reason the resistance to the new religion was not at the level of the government. The Quraysh did indeed resist the new religion to a certain extent, but if there had not been economic causes, and if the special interests of the chiefs of the Quraysh had not been at stake, the opposition to Islam that took place in Umm al-Qura would not have occurred either. As far as beliefs and ideologies are concerned, they knew that their beliefs were baseless and had no reality.

The absence of a political system in the Arabian Peninsula, or the absence of an organised religious system, was in Islam's favour. In the early periods there was no particular pressure upon Islam. Had there been such a system, it would necessarily have been contrary to the nature of Islam, and it would have risen up against Islam.

Rather, in the absence of a collective governmental and religious system, a kind of support for Islam emerged. In place of a collective system of government in the Arabian Peninsula there was a tribal system, and in this tribal system the family had importance. When the Messenger (ﷺ) rose with the call of Islam, the swords of Banu Hashim were with him, and the tribal balance that existed was in his favour. For although Banu Hashim did not accept his religion, they were certainly his supporters. Indeed, among those who accepted Islam in the early days, and whose connection was with important tribes, people feared to inflict any kind of violence upon them. Their reform and disciplinary action was entrusted to their tribes. Similarly, slaves upon whom violence was inflicted were also tortured by their masters; this is why Hadrat Abu Bakr would purchase such slaves and set them free. In this way the harshness against them would end, and they would become the clients (mawali) of Hadrat Abu Bakr. Then people would no longer meddle much with their religion. This situation gave the new religion a distinctive character. All the poor and the slaves rushed towards it.

Moreover, the Arabs possessed the qualities of bravery, personal dignity, chivalry, and a willingness to gladly embrace goodness. These are the qualities that were necessary for undertaking the responsibilities of the new religion.

Apart from these matters, all those capacities that are necessary for any civilisation and progress were present in the Arabian Peninsula at that time, and the inhabitants of the peninsula took pride in them. In the Arabian Peninsula there were ample reserves of strength, ability and personalities who were impatient to be put to use. All this was present in the heart of the unseen. Furthermore, the people of Quraysh were widely travelled and experienced throughout the world. On the one hand they travelled through the Roman kingdom, and on the other hand they travelled through the regions of the Persian Kisra, and they had seen with their own eyes all the experiences of the civilisation and culture of that time. The Quraysh's journey in summer and their journey in winter have also been recorded by the Holy Qur'an for ever:

﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer﴾ (106:1–2), ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴾ (106:3–4). Furthermore, a great store of experiences accumulated among them through various causes, so that the Arabian Peninsula would be prepared for the campaign of the Islamic revolution. When Islam came, it used all these reserves and capacities in its favour. The strength and military ability of the Arabs, which had accumulated for centuries, was unleashed. Through the key of Islam these treasures were activated. All these capacities became the wealth of Islam. This is why from the very beginning of Islam, it received such great personalities as are a great good fortune for any movement. The noble Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hold a very high station from this point of view, such as Hadrat Abu Bakr, Hadrat Umar, Hadrat Uthman, Hadrat Ali, Hadrat Hamzah, Hadrat Abbas, Hadrat Abu Ubaydah, Hadrat Sa'd, Hadrat Mu'adh, Hadrat Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and others. This group of capable companions, who accepted Islam at the very beginning, had their hearts opened by Allah to Islam, and they took up this call. Through this call these capable people became even greater, and their abilities were further refined. But their basic capacity existed even before Islam.

Here we cannot write the detailed reasons why the Arabian Peninsula was chosen for the Islamic call, why this call was protected at the start and nurtured within the Arabian Peninsula, and why Umm al-Qura and its surroundings were given precedence such that the great empires did not even turn towards it. It is because Allah wished to make the Arabian Peninsula a nursery for the new message, which was to give light to all humanity. And then Umm al-Qura was chosen so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rise from there. In any case, this would be a very long discussion and would require the pages of a separate book. Here these indications are sufficient, and beyond them further reasons can also be discovered; this is only a part of those reasons. Just as we are discovering new causes in the matter of the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) in the universe, so too further reasons concerning Umm al-Qura may be brought forward after reflection.

Thus this Qur'an was revealed in Umm al-Qura, it began its work around it, and when the whole of the Arabian Peninsula emerged from ignorance and entered Islam, and the Arabs entered Islam entirely, they raised the banners of Islam high, and they went forth with Islam into East and West, and they presented the new message and the system of Islam and the Shari'ah that came through it to humankind, in the manner that was the nature of Islam. Those who raised these banners were the most righteous people for this purpose. They took it up and spread it throughout the world. When they rose with it, the formation and shaping of Islam had already taken place in an excellent environment.

It is not a matter of chance that Allah kept the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alive until the complete dominance of Islam over the whole of the Arabian Peninsula, and that the whole of the Arabian Peninsula was purified of polytheists and the traces of shirk. Furthermore, Allah did not choose the Arabic language for this call merely by chance; rather, among the languages of the world it was the most suitable for spreading this call. It was a complete and firm language. It had a boundless capacity for expansion, and for the purposes of this call there was no better language at that time. Had it been any other language, or had there been a flaw in its formation and structure, it would not have been possible for it to fulfil the aims of the Islamic call, nor could that language have spread this call beyond the Arabian Peninsula. In short, just as the men of Arabia were suited to bear the burden of this call, so too their language was suited. (This language then became the language of the neighbouring lands.)

In short, these were the natural favourable conditions that were implicit in the beginning of this message from the Arabian Peninsula. But among all the causes, the real cause is that which the Qur'an itself has stated:

﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ (6:124). In any case, through reflection and contemplation the wisdom of God may be understood.

﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities (Makkah) and those around it, and warn them of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt: a group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze.﴾ (42:7) Warning (indhar) is mentioned very often in the Qur'an, repeated in various ways. These last two empires were enclosed within their own shells; they had their own beliefs, and there were only political ties between China and India. Because the kingdoms of China and India were enclosed within their own shells, the real influence upon the societies of the world belonged to the governments of the Caesar of Rome and the Kisra of Persia.

In that age there were two well-known heavenly religions in the world: Judaism and Christianity. Both these religions had reached a position where each had come under the influence of some government and kingdom. The influence of government had been established over these religions. The kingdom was not under the influence of religion; rather, the kingdom dominated religion. This was because distortion and alteration had occurred within these religions, and their adherents had become corrupt in conduct.

The Jews were oppressed at one time by the Romans and at another by the Persians. They had no notable position in that region. Circumstances had compelled Judaism to become merely the religion of the Jews, that is, the Children of Israel, and to shrink within itself. They neither needed nor desired to bring other nations into the religion of Judaism.

As for present-day Christianity, it was produced by the Roman kingdom. When Christianity came into existence, the Roman kingdom was in power over Palestine, Egypt, Syria and the other regions in which Christianity had spread secretly, and the Roman kingdom was persecuting it. The followers of this religion were hunted and subjected to hardships. This persecution was so severe that thousands of people were slaughtered in a cruel manner. When this period of persecution ended and the Caesar of Rome himself entered the religion of Christianity, he brought with him idolatrous myths as well. Thus the mythological philosophies of Greece entered Christianity, and the simple form of Christianity was altered. Consequently, the Christianity that came into being under the shadow of the state was entirely different from the religion that Allah revealed to Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him); rather, a new thing came into being. What happened was that the Roman kingdom recited the creed, but it was not affected by Christianity. Meanwhile, Christianity, which had not been brought under control by persecution, now came completely under control. Because of this state control, the religion broke into even more pieces, and thus a second period of persecution began: official Christianity started crushing other sects. The church was divided, and there arose the danger that the Roman kingdom itself would be divided as a result. Thus one official sect crushed the other sects, and the condition of both became such that none of them remained upon the religion of Hadrat Isa.

This was the time when Islam appeared. The aim of Islam was that humanity, which was trapped in deviation, corruption, oppression and ignorance, should be brought out of those darknesses. Islam desired to take the whole of human life under its control and to guide it upon the most luminous and correct path. It was necessary that Islam establish its supreme authority over all of humanity, so that the great revolution that Islam had in view could be brought into human life. Therefore it was necessary that Islam begin from a place that was free, and where none of the great empires of the world held power. And that the growth and development of Islam take place in circumstances in which no state would be imposed upon it that was contrary to its nature, but rather that Islam itself would be in power over that region. Keeping these aims in view, if one considers, then Makkah Mukarramah, according to the circumstances of that time, was an excellent place for the beginning of Islam, from where Islam began its universal journey, because a universal revolution was from the first day in view for Islam.

In the Arabian Peninsula in those days there was no organised government with its own laws, its own armies, its own police, which held authority over the entire Arabian Peninsula and which, relying upon its organised structure, could confront a new system of life. And the common people were not fully under its control, as was the case with the four empires of the world at that time.

Furthermore, there was no clear religion in the Arabian Peninsula such as Judaism and Christianity were, nor was there a scattered idolatry of a single kind. The beliefs and ways of life of the tribes were different. Their deities were also different: from angels, from jinn, from planets and stars, and from idols. Nevertheless, despite these circumstances, the Ka'bah and the religious leadership and dominance of the Quraysh were accepted throughout the Arabian Peninsula. Although this leadership was not a formal sovereign authority, neither in Makkah nor outside Makkah. For this reason the resistance to the new religion was not at the level of the government. The Quraysh did indeed resist the new religion to a certain extent, but if there had not been economic causes, and if the special interests of the chiefs of the Quraysh had not been at stake, the opposition to Islam that took place in Umm al-Qura would not have occurred either. As far as beliefs and ideologies are concerned, they knew that their beliefs were baseless and had no reality.

The absence of a political system in the Arabian Peninsula, or the absence of an organised religious system, was in Islam's favour. In the early periods there was no particular pressure upon Islam. Had there been such a system, it would necessarily have been contrary to the nature of Islam, and it would have risen up against Islam.

Rather, in the absence of a collective governmental and religious system, a kind of support for Islam emerged. In place of a collective system of government in the Arabian Peninsula there was a tribal system, and in this tribal system the family had importance. When the Messenger (ﷺ) rose with the call of Islam, the swords of Banu Hashim were with him, and the tribal balance that existed was in his favour. For although Banu Hashim did not accept his religion, they were certainly his supporters. Indeed, among those who accepted Islam in the early days, and whose connection was with important tribes, people feared to inflict any kind of violence upon them. Their reform and disciplinary action was entrusted to their tribes. Similarly, slaves upon whom violence was inflicted were also tortured by their masters; this is why Hadrat Abu Bakr would purchase such slaves and set them free. In this way the harshness against them would end, and they would become the clients (mawali) of Hadrat Abu Bakr. Then people would no longer meddle much with their religion. This situation gave the new religion a distinctive character. All the poor and the slaves rushed towards it.

Moreover, the Arabs possessed the qualities of bravery, personal dignity, chivalry, and a willingness to gladly embrace goodness. These are the qualities that were necessary for undertaking the responsibilities of the new religion.

Apart from these matters, all those capacities that are necessary for any civilisation and progress were present in the Arabian Peninsula at that time, and the inhabitants of the peninsula took pride in them. In the Arabian Peninsula there were ample reserves of strength, ability and personalities who were impatient to be put to use. All this was present in the heart of the unseen. Furthermore, the people of Quraysh were widely travelled and experienced throughout the world. On the one hand they travelled through the Roman kingdom, and on the other hand they travelled through the regions of the Persian Kisra, and they had seen with their own eyes all the experiences of the civilisation and culture of that time. The Quraysh's journey in summer and their journey in winter have also been recorded by the Holy Qur'an for ever:

﴿For the accustomed security of the Quraysh, their accustomed security in the caravan of winter and summer﴾ (106:1–2), ﴿So let them worship the Lord of this House, who has fed them against hunger and made them safe from fear﴾ (106:3–4). Furthermore, a great store of experiences accumulated among them through various causes, so that the Arabian Peninsula would be prepared for the campaign of the Islamic revolution. When Islam came, it used all these reserves and capacities in its favour. The strength and military ability of the Arabs, which had accumulated for centuries, was unleashed. Through the key of Islam these treasures were activated. All these capacities became the wealth of Islam. This is why from the very beginning of Islam, it received such great personalities as are a great good fortune for any movement. The noble Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) hold a very high station from this point of view, such as Hadrat Abu Bakr, Hadrat Umar, Hadrat Uthman, Hadrat Ali, Hadrat Hamzah, Hadrat Abbas, Hadrat Abu Ubaydah, Hadrat Sa'd, Hadrat Mu'adh, Hadrat Abu Ayyub al-Ansari, and others. This group of capable companions, who accepted Islam at the very beginning, had their hearts opened by Allah to Islam, and they took up this call. Through this call these capable people became even greater, and their abilities were further refined. But their basic capacity existed even before Islam.

Here we cannot write the detailed reasons why the Arabian Peninsula was chosen for the Islamic call, why this call was protected at the start and nurtured within the Arabian Peninsula, and why Umm al-Qura and its surroundings were given precedence such that the great empires did not even turn towards it. It is because Allah wished to make the Arabian Peninsula a nursery for the new message, which was to give light to all humanity. And then Umm al-Qura was chosen so that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would rise from there. In any case, this would be a very long discussion and would require the pages of a separate book. Here these indications are sufficient, and beyond them further reasons can also be discovered; this is only a part of those reasons. Just as we are discovering new causes in the matter of the divine laws (sunan Ilahiyyah) in the universe, so too further reasons concerning Umm al-Qura may be brought forward after reflection.

Thus this Qur'an was revealed in Umm al-Qura, it began its work around it, and when the whole of the Arabian Peninsula emerged from ignorance and entered Islam, and the Arabs entered Islam entirely, they raised the banners of Islam high, and they went forth with Islam into East and West, and they presented the new message and the system of Islam and the Shari'ah that came through it to humankind, in the manner that was the nature of Islam. Those who raised these banners were the most righteous people for this purpose. They took it up and spread it throughout the world. When they rose with it, the formation and shaping of Islam had already taken place in an excellent environment.

It is not a matter of chance that Allah kept the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) alive until the complete dominance of Islam over the whole of the Arabian Peninsula, and that the whole of the Arabian Peninsula was purified of polytheists and the traces of shirk. Furthermore, Allah did not choose the Arabic language for this call merely by chance; rather, among the languages of the world it was the most suitable for spreading this call. It was a complete and firm language. It had a boundless capacity for expansion, and for the purposes of this call there was no better language at that time. Had it been any other language, or had there been a flaw in its formation and structure, it would not have been possible for it to fulfil the aims of the Islamic call, nor could that language have spread this call beyond the Arabian Peninsula. In short, just as the men of Arabia were suited to bear the burden of this call, so too their language was suited. (This language then became the language of the neighbouring lands.)

In short, these were the natural favourable conditions that were implicit in the beginning of this message from the Arabian Peninsula. But among all the causes, the real cause is that which the Qur'an itself has stated:

﴿Allah knows best where to place His message﴾ (6:124). In any case, through reflection and contemplation the wisdom of God may be understood.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 42, verses 7–9 (part 2 of 2):

﴿That you may warn the Mother of Cities (Makkah) and those around it, and warn them of the Day of Assembly, about which there is no doubt: a group will be in Paradise and a group will be in the Blaze.﴾ (42:7) Warning (indhar) is mentioned very often in the Qur'an, repeated in various ways. It refers to warning people of the Day of Resurrection. In the whole history of the world, in every time and place in which human beings were born and died, Allah will gather them all on one day and then they will be divided into groups: ﴿One group will be in Paradise and one group in the Blaze﴾ (42:7). This is according to how they acted in this world, which is the abode of action, and according to the attitude they adopted during this short life.

﴿And if Allah had willed, He would have made them one community, but He admits whom He wills into His mercy; and the wrongdoers have no protector or helper.﴾ (42:8) Had Allah willed, He would have created human beings in a different manner, in which their attitude would be uniform. Their end would also be one: either all would be in Paradise or all in Hellfire. But the purpose for which Allah created this human being is that he be His vicegerent (khalifah) on this earth. The requirement of this vicegerency is that man be as he is. Special capacity is given to man, through which he is distinguished from the angels and also from the devils, whose creation is for a limited purpose and whose attitude is single. Through this capacity, some people come to guidance and light and do righteous deeds, while some turn towards misguidance and darkness and do evil deeds. Every person inclines towards one of these possibilities that are placed in his nature, and then meets the end fixed for that possibility, that is, one group goes to Paradise and another to Hell. In this way it becomes a truth that: ﴿He admits whom He wills into His mercy, and the wrongdoers have no protector or helper﴾ (42:8). The will of Allah acts according to His prior knowledge: man deserves His mercy because of his guidance, and because of misguidance he becomes deserving of error and punishment.

Earlier it was mentioned that some people had taken guardians other than Allah. Here a judgment is given that there is no protector or helper except Allah. Therefore, those whom they take as protectors and helpers are a futile act on their part, because they do not even exist. Then the question is asked:

﴿Or have they taken protectors besides Him?﴾ (42:9) This interrogative question is asked in order to draw their attention and to give the verdict that Allah alone is the Protector and Helper. He is All-Powerful. He gives life to the dead, and through this His power becomes manifest. Giving life to the dead is a very great power.

﴿So Allah is the Protector, and He gives life to the dead﴾ (42:9). After this specific manifestation of power, namely the bringing to life of the dead, the general power is mentioned:

﴿And He is over all things competent﴾ (42:9). His power is not limited merely to the giving of life to the dead.

﴿ ﴾

Then the discourse turns again to the first theme of this surah: on what standard all differences in the Islamic society are to be resolved. This revelation is the sole criterion of truth that has come from Allah; it is the straight path, and once the complete Islamic system of life has come, you must end all differences in accordance with it. Now it will not be that every person follows his own whims and desires.

The method of presenting these truths in this single paragraph is remarkable, and it needs to be reflected upon. There is a subtle and hidden connection among these truths: that the judgment concerning the differences among people rests with Allah.

*"And whatever you differ about, its judgment rests with Allah"* (42:10). Allah has sent down His judgment in this Qur'an, and this Qur'an has issued decisions concerning both this world and the Hereafter, and has laid down within it the individual and collective methods for people's lives. Their system of life, their economic system, their legal system, their political system, and the entire matter of their ethical and social conduct, the Qur'an has settled, and on these subjects it has given a sufficient and healing explanation. It has made this Qur'an the constitution of human life. It is more comprehensive and more restrictive than all the constitutions of the world. If there is a difference among them on any matter, its ruling is prepared in this Qur'an, and it has been revealed to Hadrat Muhammad (ﷺ). And he (ﷺ) established a system of life on the foundation of this Qur'an and showed it practically.

After this guidance, now begins the address of the Prophet (ﷺ), in which he announced that he entrusts all his affairs entirely to Allah, and he points to this: that this is the Lord who has granted me this principle.

*"That is Allah, my Lord; upon Him I have relied, and to Him I turn in repentance"* (42:10). This turning in repentance, this reliance, and this affirmation are recorded here from the tongue of the Prophet (ﷺ), so that they have a psychological effect on the people: behold, these are the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), the Prophet of Allah, and even he bears witness that Allah is his Lord and Ruler, that he relies upon Allah alone, turns to Allah alone, and turns to no one other than Allah. Therefore, how can other human beings and Muslims turn to anyone else in their differences, when the Prophet, who is upon guidance, brings his judgments back to Allah alone? Hence all people should, by far greater right, bring their judgments back to the Qur'an, and they should not deviate from it even for a single moment in any place. And how can they turn in their affairs to any other direction, when the Prophet (ﷺ) himself does not go in any other direction, but turns to Allah alone? For the Lord is Allah, the one in charge is Allah, the guarantor is Allah, and it is Allah who turns the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in whichever direction He wishes.

When this reality settles in the heart of a believer, his path becomes illuminated, the signs of his journey through life become clear, and therefore he does not look around in his journey at all. A brimming cup of tranquility is poured upon his heart, and confidence in his steps is spread out. Therefore he neither doubts, nor hesitates, nor is bewildered. He attains the awareness that Allah is his supporter, guardian, protector, and the one who keeps his feet firm, and that the Prophet (ﷺ) also was a traveler on this same path.

When this matter settles in the conscience and consciousness of the believer, his awareness and thinking regarding his system of life and manner of life become elevated, and therefore he cannot even imagine that there could be any other worthy method besides the Islamic system of life. Nor can he conceive that there could be any other command and judgment besides the command and judgment of Allah, to which, in the case of a dispute, one could raise one's gaze. For the guide and the Prophet also look, in their judgments, to the Shari'ah and command of Allah alone.

Now this truth is once again impressed upon the mind, so that it may penetrate thoroughly into the depths of the believer's consciousness.

*"Originator of the heavens and the earth... and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing"* (42:11). *"The Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and among the cattle as well, pairs; by this means He multiplies you. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing"* (42:11). Allah is the One who revealed the Qur'an, so that His command may be the decisive authority in your differences. He is the same Allah who is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. He is the Manager of the heavens and the earth. The law of nature that operates in the earth and the heavens is decisive in the affairs of the earth and the heavens. The matters of people's lives are in truth also a part of this universe; therefore, the implementation of the law of Allah in people's lives will in truth bring people's lives into harmony with the nature of this entire universe. Thus all human beings will walk in harmony with this universe and step in unison with it. Since in the rule of the universe Allah has no partner, therefore the rule over human life will be His.

The Allah to whose command people must return in their differences is the very Being who is your Creator. It is He who created your selves, and He knows His creation well. Then—

*"He made for you mates from among yourselves"* (42:11). Thus the foundation of your life was formed in the shape of a family; therefore He alone knows how this life can be set right and how human beings can be reformed. Allah is the One who created you in the same manner in which He created all other living creatures, and made pairs of them as well.

*"And among the cattle, pairs"* (42:11). The unity of system and the continuity of species in creation show that the Creator is one. You and the livestock pass through the process of reproduction and procreation according to this same system. Whereas the likeness of Allah is not among His creatures.

*"There is nothing like unto Him"* (42:11). Human nature accepts this principle, for if anything has been made by someone, the Creator can in no way be like it. Therefore human beings should return to the commands of their unparalleled Creator, especially in this world, in matters of their differences. They should not turn to anyone other than Allah, for He is the unparalleled Creator and Ruler. Therefore no other reference point or place of judgment can exist besides the one Reference, because there is no one like Allah.

Although there is nothing in this world like Allah, the Glorified, yet the connection between Allah and His creatures remains established and continuing. He sees and He hears, and then He judges as one who sees and hears. And in whatever disputed matter Allah judges, that judgment is then the final judgment. In the sense that the keys of the whole universe are in His hand, and have been since the time He first created it, and He established for it a natural order and put it into operation.

*"To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth"* (42:12). Therefore the authority over human beings also belongs to Him, because human beings too are a part of this universe. Hence the keys of human beings are also in His hand.

Then it is Allah who holds the authority over the expansion and restriction of people's provision. And this provision He gives them from the treasures of the heavens and the earth.

*"He extends provision to whom He wills and straitens it"* (42:12). He is their Provider, He is their Guarantor, He is the One who feeds them and gives them drink. Therefore why should they turn to anyone other than Allah to judge between them? The truth is that people should turn for judgments to the Provider and Guarantor, who manages provision and other affairs.

*"Indeed, He is All-Knowing of all things"* (42:12). Judgment can only be rendered by the One who possesses knowledge, and only His judgment can also be just... Thus the meanings of this entire discourse are interrelated and proportioned with extraordinary subtlety and refinement, so that they may impact the human heart and intellect, and strike the strings of reason and wisdom with such force that from them there arises a deeply profound, fitting, and melodious resonance.

Now this truth is once again impressed upon the mind, so that it may penetrate thoroughly into the depths of the believer's consciousness.

*"Originator of the heavens and the earth... and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing"* (42:11). *"The Originator of the heavens and the earth. He has made for you mates from among yourselves, and among the cattle as well, pairs; by this means He multiplies you. There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the All-Hearing, the All-Seeing"* (42:11). Allah is the One who revealed the Qur'an, so that His command may be the decisive authority in your differences. He is the same Allah who is the Originator of the heavens and the earth. He is the Manager of the heavens and the earth. The law of nature that operates in the earth and the heavens is decisive in the affairs of the earth and the heavens. The matters of people's lives are in truth also a part of this universe; therefore, the implementation of the law of Allah in people's lives will in truth bring people's lives into harmony with the nature of this entire universe. Thus all human beings will walk in harmony with this universe and step in unison with it. Since in the rule of the universe Allah has no partner, therefore the rule over human life will be His.

The Allah to whose command people must return in their differences is the very Being who is your Creator. It is He who created your selves, and He knows His creation well. Then—

*"He made for you mates from among yourselves"* (42:11). Thus the foundation of your life was formed in the shape of a family; therefore He alone knows how this life can be set right and how human beings can be reformed. Allah is the One who created you in the same manner in which He created all other living creatures, and made pairs of them as well.

*"And among the cattle, pairs"* (42:11). The unity of system and the continuity of species in creation show that the Creator is one. You and the livestock pass through the process of reproduction and procreation according to this same system. Whereas the likeness of Allah is not among His creatures.

*"There is nothing like unto Him"* (42:11). Human nature accepts this principle, for if anything has been made by someone, the Creator can in no way be like it. Therefore human beings should return to the commands of their unparalleled Creator, especially in this world, in matters of their differences. They should not turn to anyone other than Allah, for He is the unparalleled Creator and Ruler. Therefore no other reference point or place of judgment can exist besides the one Reference, because there is no one like Allah.

Although there is nothing in this world like Allah, the Glorified, yet the connection between Allah and His creatures remains established and continuing. He sees and He hears, and then He judges as one who sees and hears. And in whatever disputed matter Allah judges, that judgment is then the final judgment. In the sense that the keys of the whole universe are in His hand, and have been since the time He first created it, and He established for it a natural order and put it into operation.

*"To Him belong the keys of the heavens and the earth"* (42:12). Therefore the authority over human beings also belongs to Him, because human beings too are a part of this universe. Hence the keys of human beings are also in His hand.

Then it is Allah who holds the authority over the expansion and restriction of people's provision. And this provision He gives them from the treasures of the heavens and the earth.

*"He extends provision to whom He wills and straitens it"* (42:12). He is their Provider, He is their Guarantor, He is the One who feeds them and gives them drink. Therefore why should they turn to anyone other than Allah to judge between them? The truth is that people should turn for judgments to the Provider and Guarantor, who manages provision and other affairs.

*"Indeed, He is All-Knowing of all things"* (42:12). Judgment can only be rendered by the One who possesses knowledge, and only His judgment can also be just... Thus the meanings of this entire discourse are interrelated and proportioned with extraordinary subtlety and refinement, so that they may impact the human heart and intellect, and strike the strings of reason and wisdom with such force that from them there arises a deeply profound, fitting, and melodious resonance.

Now, back to the Divine revelation:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (*Fi Zilal al-Quran*, Urdu translation) on Surah 42, verses 13–16 (part 1 of 2):

Verses 13 to 16

﴿Thus does Allah, the Mighty, the Wise, reveal to you and to those before you.﴾ (42:3) This was a general indication that the source of divine revelation is one. The system that this revelation presents is the same system that the earlier messengers presented, and the direction of this revelation is the same direction that the earlier prophets followed. Now the details of this indication are being given: the way of life and the Shariah that Allah has established for the Muslims are, in their general principles, the same as those given to Nuh (Noah), Ibrahim (Abraham), Musa (Moses) and Isa (Jesus), peace be upon them. All of them were commanded to establish the one religion of Allah and not to create divisions in it, and it is your duty to remain firm on this ancient way of life of Allah. As for those who look elsewhere, seeking only the fulfilment of their own desires, do not pay them any attention. Make this religion dominant, and refute and nullify the arguments of those who dispute against this religion. Warn them of Allah's wrath and severe punishment.

There is also a very subtle connection among the sentences of this paragraph, just as we explained in the sentences of the previous paragraph.

﴿He has ordained for you of the religion that which He enjoined upon Nuh, and that which We have revealed to you (O Muhammad ﷺ), and that which We enjoined upon Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, (saying): Establish the religion and do not be divided therein.﴾ (42:13) By this, the reality is made clear, the details of which we gave at the beginning of the surah: the roots of the religions are one. In terms of time and place, it has developed in different eras. From this, a believer may have such thoughts and feelings that he considers his past to be very long, his predecessors to be very great people, and himself to be a follower and adherent of such great people: Nuh (peace be upon him), Ibrahim (peace be upon him), Musa (peace be upon him), Isa (peace be upon him), Muhammad (ﷺ). This awareness becomes firm: that this religion is a continuation of the earlier religions, and that it proceeds on the path of the prophets and messengers. And on this path it moves with great joy, even though there may be fatigue and difficulties, and he may have to sacrifice many of his worldly interests. The believer attains the firm awareness that he is a member of the caravan of great people, and that this caravan is the caravan of great people throughout the whole of human history.

That those who follow this religion of Allah have lasting peace and harmony among themselves. They stand on one permanent Shariah and one highway. There is no disagreement or enmity among them; rather, there are deep ties and connections among them. These ties and connections demand further mutual bonding and reconciliation. Thus the present state of the believers becomes linked with their past, and their past becomes joined with their present, and they all set out on one and the same path.

If the Islamic system and Shariah that Allah has prescribed for the believers and the Muslims is the same as that which was enjoined and emphasised upon Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa, peace be upon them, before it, then why do the followers of Musa and Isa (peace be upon them) fight and quarrel with one another? Then why are different sects among the followers of Isa (peace be upon him) at each other's throats? Then why do the followers of Musa and Isa (peace be upon them) harbour enmity towards the followers of Muhammad (ﷺ)? Then, what is the answer for those who claim that they follow the religion of Ibrahim, namely the polytheists of Arabia? Why are they the enemies of Muhammad (ﷺ), and why do they not gather under the banner of the Final Prophet, whose call is that all his followers should follow one religion? It was enjoined upon them that: ﴿Establish the religion and do not be divided therein.﴾ (42:13) Why do they not fulfil their duties? Why do they not give up deviation, repent from crookedness, and why do they not stand in one solid row under the banner of the last Prophet? Because after Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa and Isa (peace be upon them), now it is the turn of Muhammad (ﷺ), and this trust has now come to him.

The polytheists who dwell in Umm al-Qura (the Mother of Towns, i.e. Makkah), and who claim that they follow the religion of Ibrahim, stand against the Islamic call as opponents and adversaries. Why is this?

﴿It is hard for the polytheists, that to which you call them.﴾ (42:13) This matter is grievous to these polytheists: that among them, revelation should come down upon Muhammad, son of Abdullah. Whereas their thinking was that this revelation would descend upon some great man of the two towns.

﴿Upon a great man of the two towns﴾ (43:31), that is, that it would be revealed upon one of the great men and rulers of those two villages. But even their claim was not correct as a matter of fact: Muhammad (ﷺ), according to their own statement, was truthful and trustworthy, and he was a son of an outstanding clan of the Quraysh. He was indeed a great man.

This new call was hard for them, because if it succeeds, the era of idol worship will end, idols and the myths about idols will come to an end, and on this their leadership and authority were founded. Their personal and economic interests were tied to these notions. Therefore they embraced polytheism, and pure monotheism, which the messengers called to, weighed heavily upon them.

Furthermore, it was also grievous to them that their forefathers who had died in ignorance had died in misguidance, and that they were disbelievers and people of Hell. So they said: if our forefathers are people of Hell, then we are too. Thus they became stubborn, and out of a wrong path of hostility they took hold of it, and they deliberately prepared to throw themselves into Hell, only because they were not willing to declare their forefathers to be misguided.

The Holy Qur'an refutes their position that it is Allah's right to choose whomever He wills. In this way Allah turns His attention only to those who wish to come under His protection, and He returns those rejected people through repentance:

﴿Allah chooses for Himself whom He wills, and guides to Himself whoever turns (to Him) penitently.﴾ (42:13) So Allah chose Muhammad (ﷺ). And whoever now turns towards the path shown by Allah, Allah will guide him.

Now the address turns back to the position of the followers of the great prophets mentioned above, whom Allah sent with one religion, and who presented one religion to their people, but whose followers introduced divisions into it:

﴿And they did not become divided except after knowledge had come to them, out of envy among themselves. And if not for a word that had preceded from your Lord (to delay) until a specified term, the matter would have been judged between them. And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them are in grave doubt concerning it.﴾ (42:14) The divisions that arose among the people occurred after knowledge had come to them, and they occurred because they wanted to oppress one another. If your Lord had not already decreed that the decision would be deferred to a fixed time, their dispute would have been settled. The truth is that those who were made heirs of the Scripture after the earlier ones are in a disquieting doubt about it. In the first place, these differences were not due to ignorance. It was not because they did not know the real truth, or did not know the source of the teaching of the messengers; rather, they doubted it while knowing it well. They divided because of mutual enmity. These disputes arose because of malice and jealousy. Cruel desires compelled them to divide, and uncontrollable desires of the self forced them. This division did not occur because they had no proof for correct beliefs, or because they had no evidence from the way of life that was given to them. If they had remained sincerely firm on their true belief and Shariah, they would not have divided.

These people deserved that Allah should seize them, and that His punishment should come upon them swiftly, because of their rebelliousness and their injustice, which they did to the true religion by dividing it. But Allah, in the arrangement of the universe, had already made a decision beforehand, and a respite was granted to them until a fixed time.

﴿And if not for a word that had preceded from your Lord (to delay) until a specified term, the matter would have been judged between them.﴾ (42:14) In this way, in these differences, truth would have become truth and falsehood would have become falsehood, and the matter would have been concluded in this worldly life itself. But they were granted respite until a known time.

Those generations which became the heirs of the earlier followers who had divided, and to whom this Book came, did not receive this Book and this doctrine with certainty. Because the record of their disagreements was before them, and nothing definite and conclusive emerged from it. All the sectarian differences were confused, unclear and distressing.

﴿And indeed, those who were given the Scripture after them are in grave doubt concerning it.﴾ (42:14) Thus belief is like a firm rock around which the earth moves, yet it stands firm. A believer firmly settles upon that solid rock, and no earthquake can remove him from his place. Belief is like a star that stays fixed in its place, and despite waves and storms, the believer's eye is upon his star on the far horizon, which determines the direction. In this way a believer does not lose his way, even if he is in dark seas. But when belief and doctrine themselves become doubtful, then no one's word can remain stable. Nor can a person without belief have a stable word. Nor can such a person remain steadfast on any direction, nor can he feel satisfied on any path.

Belief and doctrine exist precisely to determine people's goal and direction, and then those who hold them lead others along that path. If they themselves are in agitation and doubt, they cannot lead anyone. "Who can awaken a sleeper but another sleeper?" When the religion of Islam came into this world, the followers of the earlier nations were in exactly this condition. Maulana Abul Hasan Ali Nadwi, in his book *Alam-e-Islam mein Mashriqiyat wa Maghribiyat ki Kashmakash* (The Conflict between Easternism and Westernism in the Islamic World), writes:

"The reality is that the leaders of the other major religions have become prey in the hands of players and gamblers, and they are under the influence of distorters and hypocrites. These religions have lost their spirit and their form. If Allah were to bring back to life the first adherents of these religions, they would not be able to recognise those religions that are attributed to their own names. Thus, while at one time these religions were givers of civilisation, culture, government and politics, now from them come disorder, corruption, differences and anarchy. Rulers are wicked in their deeds, lost in their own selves. They have no message for nations or for the world. In terms of lofty aims they are bankrupt. The springs of their lives have dried up; in the light of heavenly guidance they have no path, nor do they have any stable and firm way of life."

The famous American author George H. Danson, in his book *Emotion as the Basis of Civilization*, writes:

"In the fifth and sixth centuries of the Christian era, the world of religion was on the brink of a deep pit of destruction. Because the ideas that had helped to give birth to civilisation had come to an end, and there was no doctrine present to take the place of the religions of that time. And it was becoming clearly visible that the human civilisation which had taken four thousand years to build and develop was about to be destroyed and ruined, and humanity was about to be trapped again in ignorance and the tribal system, in which there is no law or order, because the collective order and administration that Christianity had established was about to collapse. For Christianity had become divided into sects; it had no unity and no order within it. In that period, civilisation was like a great tree whose branches spread and whose shade covered the whole world. This tree stood in a state of great weakness in the face of severe storms, and destruction was knocking at its door, when in the midst of this a person (Muhammad ﷺ) was born."

This situation arose because the bearers of the heavenly religions had begun to have severe disagreements among themselves, after knowledge had come to them. And those who became the heirs of the Book after the first people of the religions were in doubt about the truth of those very books. Because of these causes, and because of the disappearance of a centre to lead humanity throughout the world, Muhammad (ﷺ) was sent, and he was commanded to walk upon the straight path, to call people to it, and to let people say whatever they wished about his clear and manifest doctrines and his firm call. He should not turn his attention to anyone, and he should declare that this call and this system are the same that Allah gave to all the prophets and about which He enjoined them.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 42, verses 13–16 (part 2 of 2):

﴿So, to that end, invite (them), and remain steadfast as you have been commanded, and do not follow their desires, and say: "I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down, and I have been commanded to act justly among you. Allah is our Lord and your Lord. For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds. There is no argument between us and you. Allah will gather us all together, and to Him is the final return."﴾ (42:15)

Now the Islamic call was, as it were, a new leadership for all of humanity. It was a wise and rightly-guided leadership, whose system of life was clear and which possessed firm conviction. It called to Allah, worked with insight (ʿala wajh al-basirah) toward its goal, and proceeded on the command of God without any deviation. It did not follow changing aims and changing desires in its decisions. It was a leadership whose message was one, whose Book was one, whose system of law was one, and whose faith was traced back to its source of faith. And it had returned all of humanity to one important principle.

﴿And say: "I believe in whatever Book Allah has sent down."﴾ (42:15) After this, this call, this movement, rises in the world carrying the truth of the call and attains sovereign authority, so that it may act justly among people.

﴿I have been commanded to act justly among you.﴾ (42:15) This is a leadership that has authority and that proclaims justice on the earth. (The Prophet ﷺ is saying this at a time when the Islamic call is in Makkah and the caller and the movement are besieged in the Shi'b Abi Talib, and mountains of calamities are being heaped upon them; yet even there the temperament of the Islamic call, its dominant temperament, is entirely clear) (Translator). This call proclaims that the Lord is one.

﴿Allah is our Lord and your Lord.﴾ (42:15) It also proclaims that every person is responsible for his own deeds and that the accountability is individual.

﴿For us are our deeds and for you are your deeds.﴾ (42:15) Therefore, idle debate and argument should now come to an end.

﴿There is no argument between us and you.﴾ (42:15)

﴿Allah will gather us together, and to Him is the final return.﴾ (42:15)

This is one verse, yet it fully clarifies the temperament of the Islamic call. Its phrases are short, but they speak in a very plain and decisive manner. This is a call that must remain steadfast on its path and pay no regard to human desires. It must be pure in its sovereign authority over this earth so that it can act justly. It must show all humanity a straight path, which is the right path (sirat mustaqim), and this has been the path of all the messengers.

Therefore, after clarifying the Islamic call in this manner, and after a group of the believers has responded to this call, there is no longer any opportunity to give heed to the words of those who quarrel and engage in useless disputation. All their arguments have been nullified; they carry no weight and have no significance. Therefore a decisive word is now spoken concerning them, and they are left to face the severe threat of Allah.

﴿And those who dispute concerning Allah after it has been responded to, their argument is baseless in the sight of their Lord, and upon them is wrath, and for them is a severe punishment.﴾ (42:16) After the call of Allah has been answered, those who dispute about Allah's matter, their argument is baseless in the sight of their Lord, and upon them is His wrath, and for them is a severe punishment. Those who dispute concerning Allah, and whose argument is baseless in the sight of Allah, then their dispute is baseless and their proof has no standing. Their argument is rejected on earth too, and in the Hereafter they will face the severe wrath and punishment of Allah. This idle quarrel and argumentation is an appropriate punishment for them, especially when they see that the most sincere and wise people have accepted this call. Therefore, their discussion and debate come after the truth has been made clear, and they are for other purposes.

Now the direction of the discourse turns again to the original subject.
